records.text: Owens said Kash Patel was not interested and that she struggled to believe authorities did not know about the alleged French angle in Charlie Kirk's assassination; she then asserted that they did know.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: And I'm trusting Tennessean men now to keep their eyes and their ears peeled and I hope that I can be in safe hands that way because Kash Patel is just not interested and it is a struggle for me to believe that they didn't know about this French angle and the Charlie Kirk assassination. ... They did know.

verification.notes: Transcript context confirms Owens said Patel was not interested and then asserted authorities knew about an alleged French angle in Kirk's assassination. Current sources show Patel was publicly asked about Owens' allegation and said the FBI would not turn away from it, but that public response does not establish his prior interest, what the FBI knew, or that any French role existed. No public official record or independently authenticated evidence establishes advance government knowledge of the alleged angle. The accusation is therefore unverifiable rather than false.

records.text: Owens asserted that an assassination attempt against her had been coordinated and involved Israel and French intelligence agencies.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: And I was always telling the truth about the coordination of an assassination attempt, which involved Israel and French intelligence agencies.

verification.notes: Transcript context confirms Owens asserted a coordinated assassination attempt involving Israel and French intelligence. Current reporting confirms she made the allegation, but found no public documentary evidence, official confirmation, identified operational record, or independently authenticated intelligence supporting the alleged coordination. French GIGN representatives publicly rejected the claim. A denial alone does not prove the allegation false, so the underlying accusation remains attempted and unverifiable.

sources.title: Le GIGN juge ridicules les accusations de Candace Owens
sources.relevance: The report records the French GIGN response rejecting the allegation; that denial does not independently establish what occurred.

records.text: Owens said Tulsi Gabbard's office was the only government office that had responded to her warning about an alleged threat involving French intelligence agencies and Israel, and she thought the office had taken it seriously.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: I have definitively run that to the only office that has responded and I think taken my threat was wanted to respond that I should say should thought that I've been saying about the French intelligence agencies working with Israel. ... And that is Tulsi Gabbard's office. I am doing everything that I can, but I am telling you that this is very scary.

verification.notes: This is a claim about private communications and Owens interpretation of an office response. Searches found no statement, correspondence, or acknowledgment from Gabbard office confirming either a response or an assessment of the alleged threat. The text was narrowed to Owens report and appeared-to-take-seriously qualifier.

records.text: Owens cited an article as stating that Arkadi Gaydamak had been a French intelligence agent.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: He was also a factually, and you can see in this article, a French intelligence agent. Okay?

verification.notes: Transcript context confirms Owens pointed to an article and called Gaydamak a French intelligence agent. Current reporting establishes that former French officials, including Charles Pasqua and a former DST deputy director, publicly described Gaydamak as an agent or source for French counterintelligence, so an article making the cited claim exists. However, contemporaneous French reporting also documented sharply divergent intelligence-service assessments and described some claims about him as unconfirmed. The citation is real, but the underlying status is contested rather than established as an uncontested fact.

sources.title: Gaydamak's Empire and Prison
sources.relevance: The report records Charles Pasqua's statement that secret documents showed Gaydamak was an agent of the French DST.

sources.title: Le Monde, 10 April 2001: French intelligence services diverge over Arcadi Gaydamak
sources.relevance: Contemporaneous reporting shows French services reached sharply different assessments and notes that agent and arms-trafficker rumors had not been confirmed at that time.
